gap: Source variant not preserved, and no worked boundary. The entry calls itself the source's Lemmas 2--3 (handbook/parts/p15/huber-robust-location.tex line 60). It omits the source's Remark to Lemma 3 (Huber 1964, printed p.77, PDF p.5). That Remark lets the sign-change hypothesis on lambda be replaced by a weaker one: lambda exists and is finite at some xi_0 and does not vanish identically on a nondegenerate interval. Neither body 49-62 nor annex 46-83 states or derives this alternative hypothesis. The boundary it marks (lambda vanishing on an interval, where minimizing choices need not converge) is not worked. A grep finds the variant nowhere else in P15.

Source variant narrowed. The source's Winsorizing property (example (iii), printed p.79, PDF p.7) takes t_0 = T_n(x). It replaces each observation with |x_i - t_0| > k by the nearer of t_0 - k and t_0 + k, without changing the estimate T_n(x), and t_0 equals the modified mean. The entry (body 145-147) states only that, for any zero t_0, the score still vanishes at t_0 and t_0 is the modified mean. The annex (188-194) proves only that a minimizing location is preserved. It adds that the replacement 'need not preserve every tie-breaking rule for every modified sample'. The invariance of the estimate itself is neither stated nor proved: the modified sample's zero set is the single point t_0, so its midpoint estimate equals T_{n,k}(x).

Source variant narrowed: a promised case is missing. The source (Sec. 7, printed p.83, PDF p.11) says the bias bound is reached whenever H puts all its mass to the right of k + c, or to the left of -k - c. The entry states attainment only 'by contamination at any M > c_* + k' (body 286-287). The annex proves it only for H = delta_M, plus reflection (428-430). Attainment by every contaminant concentrated on [c_* + k, infinity), or its reflection, is neither stated nor proved. Yet handbook/parts/p15/robustness-and-sensitivity-of-inference-w02b-p15-071.tex lines 114-116 cite this entry for exactly that claim.

The success condition is not plainly met. Table D1-D21 in handbook/parts/p15/exchangeability-and-predictive-induction-w02b-p15-022.tex (lines 682-846) fixes the finite set of dependent sources, but not every promised proof is supplied. Rows D3, D4, D5, D5a, D7, D9, D10, D13, D14, D15, D18 and D19 are marked 'Owed to that work', and so are the general parts of D11, D16 and D20. In each case a citation stands in place of the proof. The text itself says each owed entry still needs the named work at the pages carrying the argument, and that those works are not held (lines 676-680 and 887-888). The survey's only evidence claim is D21 (Slovic and Lichtenstein 1971). It is recorded only as 'unheld and owed': no task, population, design or uncertainty is retained, and the finding 'stays owed' (lines 830-844 and 878-882). So the element 'empirical claims retain study/task/population/uncertainty' is not met. The dependent sources were fixed, but the claims that rest on them have not all been written.

Normalization and the multiplier equations are explained without presupposing a feasible optimizer (043 lines 103-153 and 296-345), and the worked distributions solve their declared problems. The component's required extent, however, is the complete construction in the original paper including its constraint and normalization derivations, and two of Jaynes's multiplier derivations are absent. (a) Jaynes's (2-15) (p. 623), the maximum-entropy estimate of the parameter derivatives of the constraint functions, equal to -(1/lambda_r) times the parameter derivative of ln Z, is not stated or derived. The forces in (3-4) rest on it. (b) Jaynes's (5-1)-(5-3) (p. 627) are absent: they make lambda_k the integrating factor of the generalized heat dQ_k and the quantity statistically conjugate to f_k, and (5-8) (p. 628) gives lambda = dS/d<E> = 1/T. Neither 166.6 nor 166.7 states, under the hypotheses of thm:p15-w02b-p15-043-existence, how the maximal entropy v_nu(c) changes with the declared values. So the source's interpretation of the multipliers is neither given nor made conditional on its premises. Only the identification lambda_1 = 1/kT appears (043 line 484).

The inferential interpretation is made conditional on the reconstructed premises (J1)-(J5) (043 lines 401-479). Those are not the paper's complete inferential argument and stated premises, which the component's required extent demands. Neither 166.6 nor 166.7 mentions ergodicity, metric transitivity or equal a priori probabilities. Missing: (a) the paper's thesis that statistical mechanics, read as inference, needs no ergodicity, metric transitivity or equal a priori probabilities (pp. 620, 621, 627, 629). Also missing are its premise that the laws of motion add no information about the state beyond what measurement supplied, and its argument that new integrals of motion, or proof that a system is not metrically transitive, would give no rational basis for excluding states the information allows unless new data are added (pp. 624-625). (b) The normative claim that maximum-entropy estimates are justified independently of experimental verification and remain the best estimates the information permits, whether or not they agree with experiment (pp. 620, 626). The interpretation is therefore conditional on an incomplete statement of the source's premises.

The success condition is 'Supply this exact entry's definitions ... and the full treatment promised by its declared status (proved)'. It is not fully met. The entry asserts V_* = 60/11 at handbook/parts/p15/huber-information-game.tex line 330, but V_* is not defined anywhere on the route: the Huber chapters define only V_k(F) and V^*(k,eps), both for the normal-contamination model (huber-robust-location.tex lines 184-185 and 199-224). The declared proof annex:p15.huber.nonnormal.examples (handbook/annex/p15/huber-information-game.tex lines 654-711) neither defines nor proves V_*. Every other logistic and Gumbel calculation in the entry is stated and proved.

The full treatment promised by the declared status proved=annex:p15.binomial.most.powerful is not supplied. The argument that no level-1/2 test is most powerful against both p=1/4 and p=3/4 writes out only the p=3/4 maximization (annex 264-269). The p=1/4 half is waved through as 'the reversed calculation' (annex 270-272), a similarly-type appeal in place of the owed step. That half is: power (3/4)a+(1/4)b=(1/4)(a+b)+(1/2)a <= 3/4 under a+b <= 1, with equality only at a=1, b=0.

The full treatment promised by the declared status proved=annex:p15.neyman.interval.construction is not supplied. The proof needs a finite upper endpoint u(x) to belong to S(x), both for S(x)=[l(x),u(x)] intersected with R and for the upper-endpoint case of the source's Proposition VII (Neyman 1937 p. 355). That step is waved through with 'The same argument puts a finite u in S(x)' (annex 445-446). Only the lower-endpoint argument is written (annex 439-444).

The full treatment promised by the declared status proved=annex:p15.binomial.confidence.coverage is not supplied. The upper-endpoint half of the exact inversion is waved through with 'Similarly ... for k=n, both are false' (annex 593-600). That half is p > u_n(k) iff F_{n,p}(k) < d for k<n, from F decreasing strictly with F_{n,u_n(k)}(k)=d, plus both conditions failing at k=n because u_n(n)=1 and F_{n,p}(n)=1>d. Both the inversion claim and the coverage bound of at least 1-alpha (annex 609-621) depend on this unwritten half.

The full treatment promised by the declared status proved=annex:p15.binomial.beta.quantiles is not supplied. The upper-limit formula u_n(k)=Q_{k+1,n-k}(1-d) depends on the lower-tail identity F_{n,p}(k)=1-I_p(k+1,n-k) for k<n. That identity is only asserted with 'Likewise' (annex 690-694). Neither route to it is written: F_{n,p}(k)=1-T_{n,p}(k+1) combined with the upper-tail identity at k+1, or derivative matching with value 1 at p=0. Only the upper-tail identity behind the lower-limit formula is derived (annex 677-689).

Argument / full treatment promised by its declared status (proved=annex:p15.confidence.test.inversion) is incomplete for the measurable converse. The claim that integrating out u 'gives jointly measurable randomized tests' rests on annex 381-390. That passage only outlines a monotone-class argument, lists its stages out of order and verifies none of them. It does not invoke the handbook's proved section-measure lemma (thm:p15-section-measures / thm:p15-tonelli, product-measures.tex 143-181). That lemma is stated for two sigma-finite factor measures, while Lambda x X carries none, so even a citation would need adapting. A sketch counts as partial.

The identified source variant is not preserved, and the corrected procedure is attributed to the source without qualification. The entry gives source Example I's sum system as A_2^U(t)={qt<=S<=(2-q)t} (half-width (1-q)t) with inversion [S/(2-q),S/q]. The held source (Neyman 1937 p. 357, eqs. (46)-(48)) instead computes (47) P=1-(Delta/theta)^2 with Delta=theta(1-alpha)^{1/2}, which gives theta(1-(1-alpha)^{1/2})<=x1+x2<=theta(1+(1-alpha)^{1/2}) and limits (x1+x2)/(1+-(1-alpha)^{1/2}) (p. 358, eqs. (50)-(51)). The two versions agree only at alpha=3/4. The entry marks its boundary choices for A_1^U and A_3^U, but it neither records the source's printed band nor marks its own band as a correction. The source variant is therefore not preserved, and attributing this band to Example I is unsupported.

The identified source variant is not preserved. The theorem is titled as the source's length comparisons, yet it states D_2=2(1-q)S/(q(2-q)) and general-alpha bounds (2-q)/4<=D_3/D_2<(2-q)/2. The held source gives the length of its sum interval as delta_2=2(x1+x2)(1-alpha)^{1/2}/alpha (Neyman 1937 p. 358, eq. (52)) and makes its comparison only at alpha=3/4 (pp. 360-362, eqs. (64)-(69)), where the two formulas agree. The source's (52) is not recorded, and the general-alpha comparison is not distinguished from the source's alpha=3/4 comparison.

The full proof promised by proved=annex:p15.neyman.normal.one.sided is not supplied. Two claims rest on annex 628-635, 'the same argument makes A^+_t=[t-sigma z_alpha,inf) the unique minimizing acceptance region': the best-one-sided criterion for the upper interval (-inf, X+sigma z_alpha], and the nonexistence argument's use of a unique minimizer on the side s<t. For this direction, three steps are not written: the Neyman-Pearson application for the decreasing likelihood ratio, the identification of the minimizing acceptance set, and its a.e. uniqueness.

Not met: 'preserve the identified source variants'. The source computes the coverage of its sum system in eq. (47), p. 357: P{E in A2(theta)|theta} = 1-(Delta/theta)^2, hence Delta = theta(1-alpha)^(1/2). Its claim (53), p. 358, says the coverage frequency is alpha for every 0<alpha<1. The handbook neither reproduces nor records either. Annex lines 29-36 derive 1-(1-Delta/theta)^2 and contradict eq. (47) silently. The treatment omits that the source's printed band has coverage 1-(1-(1-alpha)^(1/2))^2, which equals alpha only at alpha=3/4 and is about 0.397 at alpha=0.95. The rest of the component is present in complete form: the S1 empty-section failure with probability beta, the sum density, and the n-sample maximum law and interval.

Two elements of the success condition are missing for one sentence of this entry. (1) 'Construction or argument' and 'full treatment promised by its declared status' (proved=annex:p15.student.one.sided.optimal): handbook/parts/p15/student-inference.tex l.286-288 says the one-sided rejection cones 'impose no requirement that every coordinate have the same sign'. The declared proof (handbook/annex/p15/student-inference.tex l.439-500) never argues this. (2) 'Preserve the identified source variants': at the cited locator, the held NP1933 PDF p.32 (journal p.319) says the best critical cones lie in the quadrant of positive x's for a_t>a_0, and of negative x's for a_t<a_0. The entry contradicts this and does not state the regime in which each holds. The cap {Z_m>c_+} lies inside the same-sign orthant of x-m1 exactly when t_{nu,alpha}>=nu. For n=2, alpha=3/4, phi_m^+ rejects iff min x_i>m; this matches the entry's own worked interval [1,infinity) for the sample (1,3) at l.403-405. For n=3, alpha=0.95, t_{2,0.95}~2.92>=2, which matches NP's n=3 picture. So the remark needs an argument that carries this qualification, or it should be removed, and the source's quadrant description needs to be kept with its regime. Every other element of C010 is present: body l.272-285 and 288-292, annex l.441-498.

Not every stopping/error guarantee in the selected Wald 1945 extent is shown to apply to the actual selection/stopping procedure. On p.130 (pdf p.14) Wald asserts that (3.18)-(3.19) hold for the actual SPRT under dependent Gaussian autoregressive laws: x_1 and x_j - lambda_i x_{j-1} are i.i.d. N(0,1), with lambda_0 != lambda_1 in (0,1). The treatment omits this example. Its thm:p15-se-dependent (handbook/parts/p15/sequential-evidence.tex 141-151; annex 79-90) keeps almost-sure termination as a bare hypothesis and never establishes it for this or any other dependent process. So for the source's dependent procedure, the guarantee is never shown to apply to the actual stopping rule, and the [p.~130] pointer at line 150 stands in for the missing example. Also missing: the source's strict sharpening alpha'+beta' < alpha+beta for the actual nominal-boundary test when a(alpha,beta)>A(alpha,beta) or b(alpha,beta)<B(alpha,beta) (p.133). thm:p15-se-nominal (153-173; annex 92-107) states only <=.

Not every approximation in the selected source extent is explained in relation to the actual selection/stopping procedure. (i) Wald's discretization route to arbitrarily fine approximations of gamma (p.136) and of EZ_n / E(n) (p.143) for nonlattice scores is not explained. thm:p15-se-finite-recursion (parts 297-317; annex 242-248) covers only finite alphabets, and the treatment says nothing about continuous scores, including its own normal case. (ii) The source's sample-size argument is missing from def:p15-se-normal-saving (360-386). That argument says the nominal a(alpha,beta), b(alpha,beta) can only increase E_0(n), E_1(n) relative to the exact-error boundaries A(alpha,beta), B(alpha,beta), so Table 1 understates the saving of the actual equal-strength procedure (pp.133, 146, 148). (iii) Missing from def:p15-se-transform-approximation (411-463): the moment equations (4.47)-(4.50), obtained by differentiating the identity at t=0 and t=h under neglected excess; the use of (4.51) when B>0 with P(Z_n>=log A) near 1; and its mirror case B>0, A=infinity, Ez<0 (pp.149-151).

Supply this exact entry's hypotheses. The entry thm:p15-singular-contamination-stopping (handbook/parts/p15/robust-sequential-endpoints.tex 318-348) never states its observation space and does not restrict the contaminating law H. Its exact claim sup_{R in H_1} E_R N_{a,b} = E_{Q_1} N_{a,b} = (1-(3/5)^r)/(2/5) and the annex argument (annex 486-514: 'its mass p at one ranges over [2/5,3/5]'; 'If no such observation has occurred by time r, the test exits at the lower boundary') hold only when the space is {0,1}. Under def:p15-sequential-endpoint-setting (arbitrary measurable space, H any probability) and the clipped-score convention of thm:p15-huber-contamination-pair (r=1 on the common null set, so l=4/5 there), take R=(4/5)P_1+(1/5)delta_x with x outside {0,1}. R lies in H_1, and at a=3c it gives P_R(N>3)=19/125>0. Hence E_R N >= 264/125 > 49/25 = E_{Q_1} N. The failure condition 'unstated assumption' holds. Owed: state X={0,1} (or restrict H to laws on {0,1}) as a hypothesis of the entry, or compute and prove the worst-case expected size over the full stated alternative class.

The declared proof (proved=annex:p15.huber.tv.pair) is incomplete for the k_+ half of the claim 'There are unique k_-,k_+ in [0,1] satisfying ...'. Annex lines 145-146 handle existence and uniqueness of k_+ only by saying the decreasing upper-transfer function int(p_1-ks)_+ dmu 'has the analogous property'. That is a 'similarly' deferral: the property itself (1 at k=0, 0 at k=1, continuous, strictly decreasing wherever positive) is neither stated nor proved. A second, smaller gap: the argument for ell=max{c',min(c'',r)}=q_1/q_0 (annex 165-169) works out the ratio on each region but never derives that the transfer regions {k_-s>p_1} and {p_1>k_+s} are exactly {r<c'} and {r>c''}. It only asserts that they match the source's eq. (6).

Item 3 claims 'Such a choice exists, including the possible zero-risk singular case', and the declared proof does not prove this with written steps. Annex lines 313-321 restate a general bracketing fact for quantiles and support it only with 'This follows directly from the inverse-CDF construction in the preceding proof, or from the same continuity argument as thm:p15-likelihood-threshold'. That is a pointer standing in for the derivation. The cited lemma is stated and proved for P_0 with a likelihood ratio that is finite P_0-almost surely, not for the mixture M=L_0Q_0^n+L_1Q_1^n, under which T_n can carry an infinite atom. No threshold c with M(T_n>c)<=L_1<=M(T_n>=c) is derived, and neither is the randomization that fills the difference. Items 1 and 2, the item-3 minimax comparison and the zero-radius case are written in full.

The method does not state all of its hypotheses, so the failure condition 'unstated assumption' holds. The steps in def:p15-occam-method (handbook/parts/p15/occam-learning.tex lines 251-255) never require that the m training observations be independent draws with the population law P. That is the hypothesis of def:p15-occam-model at lines 20-21, and item 1 of thm:p15-occam-boundaries (lines 213-216) shows the guarantee fails without it. Even so, the conclusion at lines 257-258 claims 'the stated probability over the sample'. The steps also never require fixing a target-size bound n with l(f) <= n, which puts the target in the fixed represented class. The 'required output-size' bound n^c m^a (line 130) depends on n, and so do the sample sizes of thm:p15-occam-compression (lines 147-151) and thm:p15-occam-minimum-approximation (lines 171-173). As written, 'choose the sample size from the applicable theorem' cannot be carried out from the listed steps. The method lists the learner-side premises and the fixed-before-sampling premise as explicit steps but leaves out these data-side premises. The sibling methods do state the sampling assumption: def:p15-conc-reference-method (bounded-concentration-learning.tex 444-445) and def:p15-w02b-p15-064-method (statistical-learning-and-generalization-w02b-p15-064.tex 362-363).

Its declared status is proved=annex:p15.huber.cdf.domain, but the full proof it promises is not supplied for every assertion. The theorem (handbook/parts/p15/huber-remaining-methods.tex lines 349-350) asserts that 'smoothing alone need not preserve the original CDF bound', i.e. that Gaussian smoothing of some member of K_eps can leave K_eps. The annex proof (handbook/annex/p15/huber-remaining-methods.tex lines 329-389, construction at 356-370) only proves that mixing with Phi and then smoothing with s<=pi*delta*eps stays inside K_eps. Its only smoothing estimate is an upper bound, sup|E Phi(x-sZ)-Phi(x)|<=s/pi. No example or argument anywhere on the route shows that smoothing alone fails, so this asserted case is unproved. The rest of the theorem is proved: convexity, vague compactness, mass at least 1-2eps, and vague density of finite-information members.

The success condition 'one order-of-magnitude estimate with input ranges and an omitted-variable failure' is met only by the 073 lane-capacity estimate (measurement-dimensional-constraints-and-approximate-inferenc-w02b-p15-073.tex lines 284-375). That estimate rests on source Section 1.2, pp. 6-7, as 073 itself says at lines 28-41 and 447-449. Section 1.2 is outside the required extent 'chapter 1 sections 1.3-1.5 only for the finite estimate example'. The in-extent finite estimates in the destination body (dimensional-and-scaling-inference.tex lines 566-608: the Sec. 1.3 bill-volume and train trees and the Sec. 1.4 oil imports) have no omitted-variable failure, and only the train tree has input ranges (3200-10800 per hour, not reported as an order of magnitude). The failure condition 'report unearned digits' also holds. The oil estimate is given as 'about 3.33 10^9 barrels per year' from one-significant-figure leaf values and set against a reported 3.34 billion (lines 599-603); the held source gives 3 x 10^9 (printed pp. 15-16). The flight-range order estimate, which the text says 'discards a factor of order two', is given as 'about 9.8 10^6 m' (lines 427-433); the held source gives about 10^7 m (eq. 4.86, printed p. 133).

Half of the success condition is met: the warranted assignment contrast is stated, with its weights and premises and the unbiasedness theorem (factorial-inference-and-estimability.tex 677-726, annex 373-392; 077 404-466), and no failure condition holds. The other half, 'the additional premise for a mechanism claim', is not stated. Lines 736-741 list only kinds of evidence: process measurements with an explicit measurement model, and interventions or controls that separate the competing mechanisms. They add an unspecified category, 'assumptions connecting those observations to the causal equations', and say only that a mechanism interpretation has 'its own premises'. The passages at 075 656-662 and 077 449-450 just point back to that paragraph. Nowhere on the route is the premise itself given, meaning what must be assumed before the estimable assignment contrast can support the reflection-mechanism claim. An example would be that the checking instruction affects the response only through the reflection variable, which rules out the effort pathway of model two in thm:p15-factorial-mechanism. Another would be a stated mediation premise. The chapter promises at lines 12-13 to state 'the additional conditions under which an estimable contrast is ... an identified causal mechanism', but it delivers only a theorem that the mechanism is not identified. The route also has no link to the mediation premises in handbook/parts/p16/causal-mediation.tex.
